source_of_truth_note.issue: The nominal quantitative_growth_mechanism_supported_records CSV and JSONL files are empty.

methodology.side_assignment: Exact raw unit label takes precedence, followed by an unambiguous unit-specific source title. Mixed or generic municipal material remains unclear.

mechanism_assignment.recurring_base_or_schedule_increase: Exact text links a percentage or amount to wage, salary, base pay, hourly pay, COLA, or a wage/step schedule.
mechanism_assignment.one_time_lump_sum: Exact text identifies a one-time payment, lump sum, stipend, or bonus rather than recurring base growth.
mechanism_assignment.retroactive_payment: Exact text identifies retroactive wage or back-pay implementation.
mechanism_assignment.delayed_or_conditional_implementation: Exact text makes the pay change contingent on ratification, approval, or a later implementation event.
mechanism_assignment.unclear_or_not_recurring_base_growth: The percentage or amount concerns insurance contribution, tax, budget, utility rate, premium/assignment relation, or lacks enough context to establish recurring wage growth.

methodology.claim_boundary: All conclusions are bounded documentary mechanism statements. They are not national prevalence estimates, final wage-gap estimates, or causal effects.

implementation_or_retroactivity_layer.conclusion: The 2230 pre-rating implementation/retroactivity signals are dominated by generic effective-date or unclear timing context: 2022 records, or 90.7 percent. They must not be described as 2230 realized retroactive-pay mechanisms.

excluded_claim_ready_exception.reason: The 10 percent term expressly excludes the police officer and cannot support a police growth claim.

side_direction_conclusions: Recurring quantitative growth evidence exists on police, fire, and non-safety sides; it is not unique to public safety.
The 95-claim layer contains 48 police, 9 fire, 13 non-safety, and 2 unclear recurring-base-or-schedule records after substantive review.
Marion Township supplies a clear firefighter recurring-growth example, while Howland Road Department supplies a clear non-safety example.
Howland provides the strongest named same-municipality police/non-safety mechanism contrast, but it is not a final matched growth estimate.
Phippsburg and Tonka Bay inherited police labels are unsupported and must be corrected to non-safety or unclear.
One-time, retroactive, and delayed implementation records must remain separate from recurring base growth.
